Undulate

/UN-dyuh-layt/ - the stress falls on UN · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Undulate means to move in a smooth, wavelike motion.

All night the green curtains of the aurora undulated above the fjord.

Worked Example

Wind moved through the barley in long pulses until the whole hillside undulated — one slow wave chasing another toward the fence line.

Undulate is the smooth, continuous, full-length wave — a flag, a jellyfish, a wheat field — never a jerk or a wobble. And note the disguise: the un- is not a prefix. The word is Latin unda, 'wave,' plus endings; nothing is being negated, and there is no 'dulate' underneath.

How Undulate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ripple

ripple: small surface waves — undulate on a miniature scale

sway

sway: one body rocking side to side, no wave travelling through it

roll

roll: the broad heave of the whole mass at once

Antonyms

stiffen

stiffen: to go rigid — all wave motion lost

freeze

freeze: to stop moving altogether

How Strong Is It? — tremble → undulate → churn

tremble vs. undulate

tremble vs. undulate: To tremble is a faint, shivering motion — it stops short of undulate, which rolls in full, smooth waves.

churn vs. undulate

churn vs. undulate: Churn goes further than undulate: undulating water rolls in even waves, while churning water boils over itself in violent confusion.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of undulate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — und-

Root — und-: wave (Latin unda) — the un- here is not a prefix

Suffix — -ul-

Suffix — -ul-: little (diminutive)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb

Put it together

Put it together: The best disguise in the unit: und- is Latin unda, 'wave' — the u and n are part of the root, not a prefix — plus -ul- ('little') and -ate: 'to make little waves.' If un- meant 'not' here, undulate would be the reverse of 'dulate,' a word that has never existed. Its sibling inundate — also in this unit — is unda with the waves rolled over you.

Use the root in a new word: inundate

Use the root in a new word: inundate: Inundate — this unit's flood verb — is unda's other child: undulating water moves like a wave; inundating water arrives as one.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Undulate is halfway literary — reach for it when motion travels in smooth waves along a whole length: fields, flags, eels, hills (even a road's dips can undulate). Ripple is smaller, sway is side-to-side, wobble is unsteady. For choppy violence, churn.
